profile.reading:
Per Flexential's own individual facility page, this building (Flexential Dallas - Richardson) is located at 3010 Waterview Parkway, Richardson, TX 75080. The operator publishes a footprint of 100807 square feet and 3.75 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building, with published certifications and compliance attestations including HITRUST CSF, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, NIST 800-53, ITAR, SSAE 18. ERCOT, the Texas grid operator, forecast in July 2026 that statewide peak power demand would roughly double by 2032, from a record of about 91,308 megawatts set that July to roughly 175,000 megawatts, with ERCOT CEO Pablo Vegas citing "a massive influx of data centers" alongside population and broader economic growth as the dominant driver, per the Texas Tribune. ERCOT identified evening hours, when solar generation stops and battery reserves deplete, as the critical supply gap requiring additional natural gas capacity; Texas responded in 2023 by creating the $10 billion Texas Energy Fund loan program, which has financed 5,000 megawatts of new natural gas generation across eight projects so far, with another 2,300 megawatts under review. Texas solar capacity more than doubled between 2023 and 2025, and battery storage capacity tripled over the same period.

Texas is now forgoing at least $1.3 billion a year in sales tax revenue through its data center exemption, first enacted in 2013 when facilities were far smaller, with the state comptroller projecting the cost will reach $1.8 billion by fiscal year 2030; annual revenue loss ran only $5 million to $30 million from 2014 through 2022 before the post-2023 AI boom drove the sharp increase, according to Texas Tribune reporting. To qualify, smaller facilities of at least 100,000 square feet must create at least 20 jobs paying 120% of the area median salary and invest $200 million over five years, earning up to 15 years of exemption; larger facilities of at least 250,000 square feet must create 40 qualifying jobs, invest $500 million, and reserve 20 megawatts of transmission capacity, earning up to 20 years of exemption. The exemption covers servers, software, cooling systems, generators, plumbing, and electricity costs. State Senator Joan Huffman has called the growing cost "extremely concerning" and unsustainable, and lawmakers have signaled they may pursue repealing or narrowing the exemption, amid broader public skepticism toward new data center construction in several Texas communities.

profile.regional_context: Dallas-Fort Worth is one of the largest US data center markets, and ERCOT's 2026 forecast of near-doubling statewide power demand by 2032, driven substantially by data centers, has intensified debate over new gas generation, the Texas Energy Fund's loan-financed buildout, and the pace of solar and battery storage additions.

reading.body:
This facility publishes 3.75 MW of critical load UPS capacity in Richardson, Texas, which ranks it at the lower end of the 18 data centers in the state with disclosed power figures. Texas has 468.41 MW of published IT capacity across those 18 facilities, making this campus roughly 0.8 percent of the state's disclosed base. The operator has published a street address and square footage, enabling verification.

At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the 3.75 MW IT load would support approximately 94 racks; at 20 kW per rack, a denser mixed-workload standard, roughly 188 racks. These figures assume the published UPS capacity reflects usable IT load, though the operator does not clarify the fraction of critical load dedicated to compute versus supporting infrastructure. The facility's 100,807 square feet of technical space suggests room for growth beyond current published power.

The campus holds compliance credentials in data security (SOC 1/2/3, PCI DSS, HITRUST CSF), government standards (NIST 800-53, ITAR), and security frameworks (SSAE 18), which qualify it to host regulated workloads but do not indicate current tenant mix or specialization in GPU-intensive workloads. No power source, grid interconnection details, cooling approach, or maximum available capacity beyond the UPS rating are published.
